messages:
jen_support: Customer (enterprise) opened a support case — after upgrading to py-sdk 1.12 they started getting 401s for all requests. They say pinning back to 1.11 fixes it. Posting their repro + logs below.

jen_support: Repro steps (copied from customer):
```bash
python -m venv v && source v/bin/activate
pip install redwood-inference==1.12.0
cat > test.py <<'PY'
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(headers={ 'Authorization': 'Bearer xxxxx' })
resp = client.text.generate("hello")
print(resp)
PY
python test.py
```

jen_support: Their pip freeze: 
```
redwood-inference==1.12.0
requests==2.31.0
urllib3==2.0.4
```

jen_support: Their error (trimmed):
```
requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url: https://api.redwood.inference/v1/text.generate
  File "test.py", line 4, in <module>
    resp = client.text.generate("hello")
  File "/home/user/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/client.py", line 212, in generate
    r = self._http.post(url, json=payload)
  File "/home/user/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/http.py", line 48, in post
    return requests.post(url, headers=self._default_headers, json=json)

# Customer claims headers printed server-side show no Authorization header present
```

liam_eng: Can they share a minimal snippet showing their client init + how they set envs?

jen_support: They sent this later: 
```py
# this used to work on 1.11
client = RedwoodClient(headers={ 'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}' })
# token is a standard bearer token string
```

jen_support: They also said they tried passing api_key=... explicitly and that *did* work. So it looks like the `headers` kwarg was ignored in 1.12 but api_key still works.

liam_eng: Thanks. Quick hypothesis: in 1.12 we refactored the Client init to centralize auth and accidentally removed merging of user-supplied headers into _default_headers. We probably broke legacy `headers=` usage.

liam_eng: Short-term workaround: call RedwoodClient(api_key=token) or set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. Confirmed will authenticate.

maya_devex: Customer impact: they use a proxy that injects additional headers (x-org, trace ids) via headers=..., so switching to api_key loses that behavior. They asked for a compatible fix so headers arg still merges.

liam_eng: Agreed we should restore merging behavior. I'll open a hotfix branch to re-add header merge and add unit test. If CI green we can cut 1.12.1.

jen_support: Customer asked for ETA — they want it fixed within 24 hours or they will pin and request invoice credit.

liam_eng: I'll prioritize. Plan: revert header-change in client.init, add test for headers precedence (explicit headers override defaults), add changelog entry and a migration note. Target: patch release within next 8-12h if nothing blocks.

deploy-bot: Created ticket #SUP-4921 and CI job started: https://ci.internal/runs/98765

maya_devex: Also add a short note in the SDK migration guide: call out that `headers=` was supported historically and will be restored; suggest using `api_key` for pure auth and `headers` for extra proxy/meta headers.

jen_support: Workaround summary for the customer: 1) pin to 1.11.x OR 2) use api_key=token OR 3) set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. We'll follow up when patch is released.

liam_eng: I'll post PR link once ready.

jen_support: Thanks — I've updated the case and told them we plan a patch release.
